construct.diagnosis_or_process: Kindler epidermolysis bullosa due to FERMT1 dysfunction
construct.mechanism: FERMT1 encodes kindlin-1, a focal-adhesion adaptor involved in integrin-associated signaling and linkage of actin to membrane adhesion complexes. Loss causes mixed-level skin fragility with acral blistering early in life, childhood photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma and skin atrophy, plus mucosal disease.
construct.primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

FERMT1 encodes kindlin-1, a focal-adhesion adaptor involved in integrin-associated signaling and linkage of actin to membrane adhesion complexes. Loss causes mixed-level skin fragility with acral blistering early in life, childhood photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma and skin atrophy, plus mucosal disease. Strongest alternative resolution: Dystrophic EB is a COL7A1 anchoring-fibril disorder. Early acral blistering plus prominent childhood photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma and atrophy, mucosal disease, and biallelic FERMT1 variants are characteristic of Kindler EB.
